title: Foi feito
theme: Passive voice intro (present simple, past simple, present continuous, present perfect)
goal: Student forms passive voice in basic tenses to shift focus from agent to recipient or to depersonalize information.
connects_to: M16 (Passive voice expanded) — modal passives, future passive, "by + agent".
module_chunks: The book is read (present simple passive)
The book was read (past simple passive)
The book is being read (present continuous passive)
The book has been read (present perfect passive)

units.title: It is made
units.real_life_context: You describe general facts where the agent is unknown, unimportant, or implied.

grammar.explanation: Passive present simple = "am/is/are + past participle". "English is spoken" — foco na língua, não em quem fala. Forma passiva clássica para fatos gerais.

grammar.sentence: The factory _____ a thousand cars a year.
grammar.explanation: "The factory produces" — ativa, pois a fábrica é o agente real. Se fosse passiva: "A thousand cars are produced by the factory".
"Coffee is grown" — café é o que recebe a ação. Foco no produto, não em quem planta. Passive present simple.
Plural "cars" → "are made". "Cars are made in the factory" — passive present simple, plural.
"Are made in Italy" — passive plural. Foco nas camisas (recipient), não em quem fabrica.
"Spanish is spoken" — passive present simple singular. Foco na língua.
"Rice is grown in Asia" — fato geral, agente impreciso, passive natural.

grammar.sentence: English is speak in many countries.
grammar.answer: English is spoken in many countries.
grammar.explanation: Passive precisa de past participle, não base form. "Speak" → "spoken". "Is speak" não funciona.

grammar.sentence: Cars is made in the factory.
grammar.answer: Cars are made in the factory.
grammar.explanation: Concordância: "cars" (plural) → "are made". Singular seria "the car is made".

grammar.passage: English is spoken in many countries around the world. Coffee is grown in Brazil and Colombia. These shirts are made in Italy. Rice is grown mostly in Asia.
grammar.question: Where is coffee grown?
grammar.answer: in Brazil and Colombia (or "Brazil and Colombia")
grammar.explanation: The text says "Coffee is grown in Brazil and Colombia".

listening_speaking.text: English is spoken in many countries.
These shirts are made in Italy.
The form is filled out online.

units.title: It was built
units.real_life_context: You describe historical events, completed works, or past origins where the agent is general or known.

grammar.sentence: The pyramid _____ thousands of years ago.
grammar.explanation: Passive past simple = "was/were + past participle". "The pyramid was built" — passive singular passado.

grammar.sentence: The Mona Lisa _____ by Leonardo da Vinci.
grammar.explanation: "Was painted by..." — passive past + "by + agent" para mostrar quem fez.
Plural "bridges" → "were built". Passive past simple plural.
"The package was delivered" — passive past simple, foco no pacote (recipient).
"Was published in 1925" — passive past, ano específico.
Plural "two cars" → "were damaged". Passive past simple plural.
"The decision was made" — passive past, foco na decisão.

grammar.sentence: The Mona Lisa was paint by Leonardo.
grammar.answer: The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo.
grammar.explanation: Após "was/were" sempre past participle, não base form. "Paint" → "painted".
"Bridges" (plural) → "were built". "Was" é só para singular.

grammar.passage: The pyramids were built thousands of years ago. The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo da Vinci. These bridges were constructed in the 19th century. The package was delivered yesterday morning.
grammar.question: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
grammar.explanation: The text says "The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo da Vinci".

listening_speaking.text: The pyramids were built thousands of years ago.
The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo.

units.title: It's being done
units.grammar_focus: Present continuous passive (am/is/are being + past participle)
units.real_life_context: You describe ongoing processes — what is happening right now to something or someone.

grammar.explanation: Passive present continuous = "am/is/are + being + past participle". "Is being repaired" — ação acontecendo agora, foco na estrada.
Plural "reports" → "are being written". Ação em progresso, passive.
"Is being repaired today" — em processo hoje. Passive present continuous.

grammar.sentence: The houses _____ next to the park.
grammar.explanation: Plural "houses" + ação em curso → "are being built".
"Are being washed" — em processo agora, plural.
"Is being cleaned right now" — ação em curso, singular.

grammar.sentence: The new policy _____ at this moment.
grammar.explanation: "Is being discussed at this moment" — discussão em andamento.

grammar.hint: Para ação em curso, precisa de "being"
grammar.answer: My car is being repaired today.
grammar.explanation: "Is repaired" sem "being" = present simple passive (fato geral). Para AÇÃO EM CURSO HOJE, precisa "is being repaired".

grammar.sentence: The houses being built next to the park.
grammar.answer: The houses are being built next to the park.
grammar.explanation: Estrutura completa: "are being built" — verbo to be conjugado + being + past participle. Não dá pra omitir o "are".

grammar.passage: The road is being repaired this week. The reports are being written right now. My car is being fixed today — I'll get it back tomorrow. The new houses are being built next to the park.
grammar.question: What is being built next to the park?
grammar.explanation: The text says "The new houses are being built next to the park".

listening_speaking.text: My car is being fixed today.

units.title: It has been done
units.grammar_focus: Present perfect passive (has/have been + past participle)
units.real_life_context: You describe completed actions with present relevance, with focus on result not agent.

grammar.explanation: Passive present perfect = "has/have + been + past participle". "Has been delivered already" — ação completa com relevância presente.
Plural "three schools" → "have been built". Period "this year" inclui o presente → present perfect passive.
Pergunta com "yet" → present perfect passive. "Has the report been finished yet?".
Plural "decisions" + "recently" (período até agora) → "have been made". Passive present perfect.
"Has been released already" — lançamento completo com efeito presente. Singular.
Plural "many books" → "have been published". Period "this year" → present perfect.
"Has been done" — "do" → past participle "done". Forma irregular.

grammar.answer: The package has been delivered already.
grammar.explanation: Present perfect passive precisa de "has/have BEEN + past participle". "Has delivered" sem "been" não é passivo.

grammar.sentence: Three new schools has been built.
grammar.answer: Three new schools have been built.
grammar.explanation: Concordância: plural → "have". Singular seria "the school has been built".

grammar.passage: The package has been delivered already. Three new schools have been built this year. The report has been finished and sent to the client. Many decisions have been made recently.
grammar.question: What has happened to the report?
grammar.answer: it has been finished and sent (or "finished and sent")
grammar.explanation: The text says "The report has been finished and sent to the client".

listening_speaking.text: Three schools have been built this year.
The new car has been released.

units.title: All passives together
units.grammar_focus: Integration of present simple, past simple, present continuous, present perfect passive
units.real_life_context: You mix passive tenses fluently in real description.

grammar.explanation: Fato geral atual → present simple passive. "English is spoken" — habitual/factual.

grammar.sentence: The pyramid _____ thousands of years ago.
grammar.explanation: Tempo específico passado → past simple passive. "Was built thousands of years ago".
"At this moment" → ação em curso → present continuous passive. "Is being repaired".
"This year" inclui presente → present perfect passive. "Have been built".
Fato atual contínuo → present simple passive plural.
"Yesterday" → past simple passive singular.
"Right now" → present continuous passive. "Is being built".

grammar.sentence: The book is wrote by a famous author.
grammar.answer: The book is written by a famous author.
grammar.explanation: Verbo irregular "write" — past participle é "written", não "wrote".
Plural sempre "were" no past simple passive.

grammar.passage: English is spoken worldwide. The pyramid was built thousands of years ago. The road is being repaired this week. Three new schools have been built this year. These shirts are made in Italy.
grammar.question: When was the pyramid built?
grammar.explanation: The text says "The pyramid was built thousands of years ago".

listening_speaking.text: The pyramid was built thousands of years ago.
Three schools have been built this year.

cross_unit_consolidation: Present simple passive: is/are + past participle (fatos gerais)
Past simple passive: was/were + past participle (eventos passados)
Present continuous passive: is/are + being + past participle (ações em curso)
Present perfect passive: has/have + been + past participle (ações com efeito presente)
Sempre "to be" conjugado + past participle (nunca base form após "to be")
